simple.meaning: כֵּן (kên) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a gnat.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 8:12. The surrounding context includes death, land.

definitions.full: H3654. ken IV. כֵּן (?), כִּנָּם כִּנִּם, noun [masculine] , meaning dubious; either gnat, gnats, gnat-swarm (so ᵑ9 ᵐ5 <TOPIC:Philo Judaeus> Philo Vita Mos. i, p. 97 , <TOPIC:Origen>Origen Hom. 4, 6 in Ex. , and most moderns), or [louse,] lice (so ᵑ7 ᵑ6 Jos Ant. ii. 14 . 13 Boch Hieroz. II, ii, 572 f. , as Late Hebrew כִּנָּה , plural כִּנִּים = maggots , and especially lice ) — absolute perhaps כֵּן Isa 51:6 (see below); plural כִּנִּים Exod 8:13 ; 8:14 ; Psa 105:31 , כִּנִּם Exod 8:12 ; 8:13 ; 8:14 has, also, כִּנָּם probably a mere Masoretic device for כִּנִּם (compare Di), on account of preceding וַתְּהִי (on which see Ges § 145 . 4 Da Synt. § 116 ); ⅏ has כנים throughout: — of Egyptian plague 8:12 ; 8:13 (twice in verse); 8:14 (twice in verse) (all P), hence Psa 105:31 ; יְמוּתוּן כְּמוֺכֵֿן Isa 51:6 like a gnatswarm (?) shall they die (compare Di Du; Weir Che read כנים , compare Buhl p. 355 ; > Brd De like this ). Note. — Nö M 54 Ba NB § 15, ES 53 Buhl Ges HWB ed. 12 connect this word etymologically with Aramaic כלמתא vermin , Ba and Buhl also with Assyrian kalmatu, id. [Dl HWB 333 ], and even with Aramaic קלמתא , , Arabic , etc., Ethiopic louse ; but these connections, as well as that with Late Hebrew כְּנִימָה , all involving radical מ , are most improbable
definitions.rootNote: from 3661 in the sense of fastening; (from infixing its sting; used only in plural (and irregular in Exodus 8:17,18; Hebrews 13:14))
